analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Thursday Thoughts 12 Nov 2026
key_insights: Crude has weakened over the last month (WTI -9%) while large-cap E&Ps held up better (-4% on average).

Medium-term oil views are more cautious: Hormuz flows have recovered, supply growth and upward revisions to balances for the next couple of years (LATAM and Canada more in focus on the desk), and fewer questions about the right oil and products risk premium.

DVN is the most debated stock on the desk after its 3Q print. Defenders cite the strategic review being done, a ramping buyback, and more favorable positioning (less well owned), which they think lets the stock hold in a crude flush.

OXY investor questions have shifted from rate of change, the new debt target and operations to how much the stock could underperform the group if crude flushes over the next few weeks. EOR discussion on the call is not seen as a surprise, since EOR has been part of the OXY story for some time.

COP had a couple of downgrades in recent days. Pushback centers on relative performance (best performing Large Cap and US Major) and on it being too early to play for a FCF inflection that is a couple of years away. Buybacks are expected to rise in 4Q, and the stock trades at a high single digit FCF yield on GS numbers.
The desk still sees a preference for Large Cap and quality in this tape, but senses the level of offense being played in COP has slowed.

Uranium investor inbounds have ticked up slightly over the last week. Questions cover how light positioning is, direct U3O8 vs miners vs supply chain, whether spot and term commodity moves matter now, and what it takes for the narrative to disconnect from the data center story.

GS states the fundamental uranium story has nothing to do with data centers, AI or power infrastructure. Dedicated investors are looking at P/NAV relative to the last cycle, headlines on uprates are constructive, and nuclear is seen as having bipartisan support.
CME is pursuing a new physical uranium contract as prices climb, flagged the day before.

market_movers.rationale: Other firms downgraded COP over the last few days, citing relative performance and a FCF inflection that is a couple of years away. This note reports those downgrades and does not issue one.

sector_views.rationale: E&Ps held in better than crude over the last month, medium-term oil views are more cautious on supply growth, and the desk sees a preference for Large Cap and quality.
Investor inbounds are rising and positioning is light. GS says the fundamental story is separate from data centers and AI power demand.

earnings_insights: DVN reported 3Q and is the most debated stock on the desk afterward. The note gives no figures.
OXY discussed EOR on its earnings call. The note gives no figures.
COP buybacks are expected to trend higher in 4Q, with a high single digit FCF yield on GS numbers.
risk_factors: A crude price flush over the next few weeks could cause OXY to underperform the group.
Supply growth and upward revisions to oil balances for the next couple of years.
The uranium narrative is tied to the data center story, and the desk wants it to disconnect.
vol_and_positioning: DVN positioning looks more favorable, as it is not as well owned as before.
Positioning in uranium is light, according to investor questions on the desk.
geopolitical: Hormuz flows have recovered, and fewer investor questions are coming in about the right risk premium for oil and products.
